主要内容: A survey by Genesys indicates U.S. workers believe jobs in Manufacturing (43%), Retail/Checkout Clerks (40%), Telemarketers (38%), and Data Entry (37%) are most likely to shrink due to AI expansion. Two-thirds (67%) of respondents say they are not afraid AI/bots will replace their jobs within 0-10 years. Employees in Education/Training and Doctor/Nurse/Caregivers are least afraid, while those in Media and Assembly Line/Manufacturing jobs are most concerned. Human Resources identified Data Entry and Retail/Checkout jobs as most at risk. Customer Service workers selected Retail/Checkout Clerks and Telemarketers as most vulnerable. Only 16% of respondents see Transportation jobs as at risk, despite predictions about autonomous vehicles. Food Service jobs are also seen as less threatened, despite media coverage of automated restaurants. Merijn te Booij, Genesys' chief marketing officer, emphasized the need for human-AI collaboration to enhance productivity and job satisfaction. The survey, which included 1,001 U.S. employees, highlights concerns about AI's impact on employment across industries.
